data.hypothesis: The baseline is correct and averages 3.494 μs across three samples, but there is no profiling evidence isolating its bottleneck. A 256-thread flattened launch keeps warp lanes on contiguous x elements for this 64-wide row while replacing shared-memory staging and two block barriers with eight explicitly unrolled direct-global neighbor loads. Avoided synchronization may help, while repeated neighbor loads may offset that benefit; latency must be measured.

memory_lessons.applicability: This is a baseline fact for the supplied 64³ target; it does not identify the source of runtime cost.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline is valid, with three event-latency samples averaging about 3.494 μs; no profile or child measurements establish whether synchronization or memory traffic dominates.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate the direct-global candidate with the independent oracle, then compare its full-run event latency under the same protocol.

data.notes: This candidate uses one 1D launch with 256 threads per block, one output per thread, no shared memory or block-wide barriers, and no added allocation or launch. For every neighbor offset it preserves the baseline halo mapping: out-of-range rows are adjusted by my-1, including the endpoint-row convention. The baseline is the only measured program in the catalog; this candidate has not been measured.
transformations: Replace the active shared-memory y-derivative with a flattened 1D direct-global kernel assigning one output to each thread.
Map adjacent warp lanes to contiguous x positions using 256-thread blocks, which align to the 64-element row width.
Explicitly calculate all eight y-neighbor row indices and reproduce the baseline's my-1 halo wrap for each offset.
Retain the existing coefficients, arithmetic form, one-kernel-call entry point, and output coverage without extra allocation.
